construct: LDLR loss of function reduces hepatic clearance of circulating LDL particles. LDL receptors normally bind apoB-100-containing LDL and mediate receptor-dependent uptake, so impaired receptor function causes marked lifelong elevation of LDL cholesterol and premature atherosclerosis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Marked lifelong LDL elevation, tendon xanthomas, premature familial coronary disease, and LDLR loss of function identify reduced receptor-mediated hepatic LDL clearance as the tested mechanism.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: ABCA1, LCAT, LPL, and MTTP are genuine lipoprotein pathways, but none mediates LDLR-dependent hepatic uptake. The explicit LDLR loss-of-function variant makes impaired receptor-mediated LDL clearance uniquely correct.
